scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-WRONG-BILLS-AUTOFIX.statement: Dispute surge is caused by a billing-process defect producing incorrect bills, and the right fix is an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-corrects whatever generates the wrong bills.

H-AMI-READ-DEFECT.statement: A defect or disruption in AMI read delivery or validation (MDMS) since August increased estimate substitutions or wrong register reads feeding the billing system, driving the dispute surge.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter-read completion or upload quality degraded since August (missed routes, late/invalid uploads), increasing estimated bills and resulting disputes.

H-RULE-CHANGE-MISCLASSIFICATIO.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August caused valid reads to be rejected or misclassified, producing incorrect bills and disputes.

H-TICKET-INTAKE-ARTIFACT.statement: The apparent doubling of dispute tickets reflects a change in CRM ticket categorization, intake, or SLA process since August rather than an actual increase in incorrect bills.

H-BILLCALC-DEFECT.statement: A billing calculation or import defect affecting bills with ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads is driving the larger share of the dispute surge, independent of estimate substitution.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-NOT-BOTTLENEC.statement: Ticket response speed is already within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d), so the dispute problem is driven by ticket volume/root cause of wrong bills, not by slow responses, making an auto-answer feature of low value on its own.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high-consumption (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), causing valid actual reads to fall back to estimate substitution and producing disputed bills.

H-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT.statement: Billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw register values against 12-month m3 consumption history without unit scaling, causing valid high-register reads (regardless of ACTUAL or ESTIMATED path) to be misclassified as high-consumption and rejected.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Monthly CRM dispute counts show ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 (610, 590) rising to 1180 in Aug and 1260 in Sep 2026, confirming the dispute volume roughly doubled starting August and remained elevated into September. This quantifies the timing and magnitude of the surge but does not indicate whether it stems from actually wrong bills, a read/validation defect, or a ticket-intake/process change.

A query of billing-db's tariff change log returned zero records, meaning no tariff/rate changes occurred during the period of interest. This rules out a tariff rate adjustment as the cause of the wrong bills behind the dispute surge; it does not speak to AMI reads, field reads, import validation rules, or ticket-intake process, which remain open candidate causes.

Of disputed bills broken down by read type, 1785 have ACTUAL (meter-read) type versus 1240 ESTIMATED, so the majority of disputed bills are on bills with actual (non-estimated) meter reads, not estimate substitutions.

CRM response-time metrics (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d against a 3.0d SLA, 2440 tickets) show dispute tickets are already being answered within SLA on average; this is an observation about handling speed, not about whether underlying bills are wrong. It undercuts the premise that response-time/backlog pressure is the operational problem needing an auto-answer agent, independent of whatever is causing the wrong bills.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's unverified statement that no tariff change occurred this year corroborates the already-established authoritative finding (E-02) that no tariff/rate change log entries exist since August; it adds no new causal information and does not touch any system (AMI, field reads, import rules, ticket intake) still under investigation.

Field route completion was 88% against a 95% target for Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, meaning field manual reads fell short of target during the dispute-surge window. This is consistent with missed routes forcing estimate substitutions, but it does not by itself explain the dispute majority, which E-03 shows sits on ACTUAL-read bills rather than ESTIMATED ones.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims field reading has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and the affected customers to receive estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder explanation that offers a staffing-shortage mechanism consistent with the below-target route completion in E-06, but it does not address why the majority of disputed bills (E-03) carry ACTUAL rather than ESTIMATED read type.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (§4.2) confirms that route priority changes may be requested by the utility but are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update rather than revealing anything new about the dispute-surge root cause.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-09) returns only account_id and route fields for 320 accounts across 40 distinct routes — it lacks the read_type, tariff, and import-status fields the pull was meant to supply, so it cannot directly link these accounts to disputed bills or test a causal mechanism. It only establishes that the current estimated-account population (320) is small relative to the 9200 manual-read account base (E-06) and the 1785 ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-03).

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) lists 14 behind-schedule routes with per-route completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), giving route-level granularity on the already-known below-target field completion (E-06). It adds detail but no new causal signal linking field-read degradation to the ACTUAL-read-dominated dispute majority (E-03), so it does not change the root-cause picture.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor-side engineer) states that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471. This is an unverified stakeholder claim that, if true, could unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export:read_events_for_disputed_estimated query needed to test H-AMI-READ-DEFECT and resolve VOB-U-DEFECT-LOCUS; it supplies no AMI read-event data or causal evidence itself.

Of the AMI read events behind disputed ESTIMATED-type bills, 1184 (95%) show a read was received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected at import under status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 show no AMI read received at all. This indicates the disputed-ESTIMATED population is dominated by a billing-import validation rejection of valid reads, not by AMI non-delivery or field-staffing-driven estimate substitution.

E-13.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The billing-config rule-change log (E-13) shows validation rule BV-17 — a high-consumption check that compares raw register value against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling "none" — was deployed 2026-08-01, exactly coinciding with the dispute-surge onset (E-01); the only other logged change, BV-09, is a cosmetic label edit from March 2026 and is causally irrelevant. This supplies a concrete, dated billing-import mechanism (a possible unit-scaling defect) that could produce the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections already observed in E-12.

MDMS firmware metadata shows meters on firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) record register readings in units of 0.1 m3, while v3.x meters record in plain m3; this firmware-to-unit mismatch is a concrete mechanism explaining why BV-17's unit-scaling='none' raw-value-vs-m3-history comparison would systematically flag v4.2 meter reads as high-consumption, matching the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern already seen in E-12 (which cites firmware v4.2).

U-DEFECT-LOCUS.question: Does the actual-read billing defect originate in AMI read delivery/validation (vendor MDMS) or in billing import/calculation (billing-db)?
U-DEFECT-LOCUS.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation targets the AMI vendor pipeline or internal billing calculation logic, and who would execute/approve the eventual fix.
U-DEFECT-LOCUS.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned MDMS export access (currently blocked: mdms-export is DEGRADED with an ACCESS_PENDING hold) and compare AMI read events against disputed ACTUAL-read bills; cross-check against the billing-config rule-change log.
U-DEFECT-LOCUS.safe_placeholder: Run AMI and billing-calc diagnostics in parallel; do not commit to or auto-execute any remediation until the defect is localized.
U-DEFECT-LOCUS.resolution: For the AMI reads underlying disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184/1240 show the read was received and exported but rejected at billing import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), vs only 56 with no AMI read received, indicating the dominant defect locus for this subset is billing import/validation rather than AMI read delivery (E-12); whether the same mechanism explains the larger ACTUAL-read dispute majority remains untested.

U-INTAKE-VS-REAL-INCREASE.question: Is the doubling of dispute tickets a real increase in incorrect bills, or partly an artifact of a CRM ticket categorization/intake process change since August (H-TICKET-INTAKE-ARTIFACT, not yet tested)?
U-INTAKE-VS-REAL-INCREASE.decision_impact: If intake-process-driven, the wrong-bills premise overstates the problem and remediation should target CRM categorization rather than the billing/AMI pipeline.
U-INTAKE-VS-REAL-INCREASE.resolution_path: Review CRM intake/categorization rule history around August against the raw dispute volume trend.
U-INTAKE-VS-REAL-INCREASE.safe_placeholder: Treat dispute-volume figures as provisional for sizing purposes until intake-process stability is confirmed.

U-DATA-COMPLETENESS.question: Are DA-BILL, DA-MDMS, DA-ROUTE and DA-RULES complete enough (all currently marked completeness UNKNOWN) to support a root-cause conclusion?
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS.decision_impact: Incomplete source data could bias the AMI-vs-billing-calc attribution and the sizing of success metrics.
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS.resolution_path: Request a completeness assessment from the ORG-UTIL and ORG-AMI data owners for each asset before finalizing root cause.
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS.safe_placeholder: Label diagnostic findings as provisional pending completeness confirmation.
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS.resolution: For the DA-RULES component of this unknown, E-13 is an AUTHORITATIVE, COMPLETE billing-config query returning full rule-change records (BV-17, BV-09); DA-BILL, DA-MDMS and DA-ROUTE completeness remain unaddressed by this observation.

U-DEFECT-SCOPE-ACTUAL.question: Does the same BV-17/unit-scaling rejection mechanism confirmed for disputed ESTIMATED-type bills (E-12) also explain the larger disputed ACTUAL-read-type bill majority (1785, E-03)?
U-DEFECT-SCOPE-ACTUAL.decision_impact: Determines whether the billing-import fix must be scoped only to the estimate-substitution path or extended to directly affect ACTUAL-read bills; changes the scope and expected size of the remediation.
U-DEFECT-SCOPE-ACTUAL.resolution_path: Query billing-db import status/rejection codes for disputed ACTUAL-read bills and compare against the BV-17 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern already confirmed in E-12.
U-DEFECT-SCOPE-ACTUAL.safe_placeholder: Scope any BV-17/unit-scaling remediation strictly to the confirmed ESTIMATED-read rejection path until the ACTUAL-read population is tested with evidence.

U-TICKET-INTAKE-ARTIFACT.question: Is the doubling of dispute tickets a real increase in incorrect bills, or partly an artifact of a CRM ticket categorization/intake process change since August (H-TICKET-INTAKE-ARTIFACT, untested)?
U-TICKET-INTAKE-ARTIFACT.decision_impact: If part of the volume increase is an intake artifact, M-DISPUTE-VOL reductions after remediation would overstate success and the dispute-surge symptom itself needs re-measurement.
U-TICKET-INTAKE-ARTIFACT.resolution_path: Audit CRM ticket intake/categorization configuration for any process change coinciding with August 2026.
U-TICKET-INTAKE-ARTIFACT.safe_placeholder: Treat the current M-DISPUTE-VOL reading as provisional and do not claim full remediation success from ticket-count reduction alone until intake-process stability is confirmed.

A-ACTUAL-SHARE-SCOPE.statement: The ACTUAL vs ESTIMATED breakdown in E-03 is assumed to cover the same Aug-Sep dispute-surge population measured in E-01, though the query result does not state an explicit date range.

A-DEFECT-NOT-VOLUME-ARTIFACT.statement: The skew toward ACTUAL-read bills among disputes (E-03) is assumed to reflect a read/billing defect rather than simply a larger underlying population of ACTUAL-read accounts in general.

A-FIELD-GAP-SECONDARY.statement: The field route-completion shortfall (E-06) is assumed to be a real but secondary issue, not the primary driver of the dispute surge, since disputes skew to ACTUAL rather than ESTIMATED reads (E-03).

A-TIMING-COINCIDENCE.statement: The temporal coincidence between BV-17's 2026-08-01 deployment and the August dispute-volume doubling (E-13, E-01) is assumed to be causal rather than merely co-occurring with some other unidentified August change.
